title: Optimize NCCL overlap, KV cache sharding, and continuous batching for tensor-parallel multi-GPU runtime
author: Ethan Kim
release_notes: Tensor-parallel NCCL scheduling and KV-cache/continuous-batching improvements: reduced p99 latency and increased throughput for multi-GPU inference. No user-facing API changes.
body:
Motivation: Multi-GPU tensor-parallel workloads at Redwood showed variable overlap between communication (NCCL collectives) and local compute, leading to p99 tail latency regressions on long-context workloads. In addition, KV cache sharding and continuous batching introduced coordination overhead that increased stragglers under high-concurrency regimes. This PR introduces a set of coordinated runtime changes to improve overlap, reduce synchronization points, and make KV-cache/continuous-batching more resilient to skew.

What this PR does: - Rework NCCL stream and priority assignment in runtime/nccl to ensure comm streams are scheduled with higher priority relative to blocking kernel streams for the common TP collective patterns. - Introduce async-aware collective wrappers that prefer non-blocking launches and only synchronize when required by the tensor-parallel algorithm. - Add explicit kernel preemption points and a fast-path bypass for small-kernel work to avoid unnecessary syncs. - KV cache sharding: move from coarse global barriers to per-shard progress tracking; shard owners can service continuous-batcher requests independently with lightweight handshakes (no global CUDA device sync). - Continuous batching: improve batch cutoff heuristics, backpressure signals to clients, and add a speculative flush path when a shard is known to be idle for >10ms. - Add metrics and internal tracing (per-collective latency, stream idle time, kvcache shard stalls) and a benchmarking harness for TP+KV workloads.

Checklist: - [x] Rework NCCL stream mapping and priority config (runtime/nccl/*) - [x] Add async-collectives and non-blocking wrappers (runtime/nccl/async_collectives.*) - [x] Kernel scheduling tweaks and preemption points (runtime/kernels/*, scheduling/*) - [x] KV cache shard manager + per-shard progress (runtime/kvcache/shard_manager.*) - [x] Continuous batcher improvements and heuristics (runtime/batching/continuous_batcher.*) - [x] Unit + integration tests for multi-GPU TP paths (tests/integration/*) - [x] Benchmarks and docs (runtime/benchmarks/*, docs/perf/*)

Compatibility and rollout: No public API changes. Changes are guarded behind a runtime config flag `tp_nccl_overlap_v2` and `kvcache_shard_progress`. Default rollout is disabled; we enabled the flag in internal perf clusters and after validation toggled it on for main. The PR includes a brief migration note in docs.

Testing and validation: - Microbenchmarks: synthetic TP model runs across 2/4/8 GPUs used to validate overlap and stress KV-cache. - End-to-end: integration tests with continuous-batching + KV cache enabled, ran against both NCCL and mock-collective backends. - CI: unit + integration consistently pass; real-HW benchmarks run on internal perf fleet.

Results summary (see `runtime/benchmarks/tensor_parallel_nccl_bench.py`): - p99 latency reduced by ~18% on average (example: 124ms -> 102ms) for 4-GPU TP inferencing on our long-context Llama-variant tests. - Overall throughput improved ~22% for batched inference under typical request mixes. - KV-cache miss/stall events reduced by ~65% after per-shard progress tracking.

Rollout plan: - Step 1: land PR behind flags (this change) - Step 2: enable on internal perf clusters and smoke test (2 days) - Step 3: enable in canary for non-sensitive tenant traffic (1 week) - Step 4: enable broadly with monitoring and rollback on regressions

Notes: - We observed one flaky test related to CUDA stream ordering on older driver images; the PR adds a guard and a skip for driver < 535. - There are small kernel changes that affect scheduling; benchmarks validate numeric parity for inference outputs.

Related: ENG-5173, ENG-5210, SUP-1209.

review_comments: Ava Patel: Can we avoid a global CUDADeviceSynchronize() in the new shard manager? Observed several spots that call sync during error paths.
Ethan Kim: Addressed in latest commit (c3e7b1a) - replaced global sync with per-shard progress polling and added fast-fail path.
Miguel Santos: The priority mapping looks good, but please add a feature-flag gate so we can roll back quickly.
Ethan Kim: Added `tp_nccl_overlap_v2` gate in deploy/config/runtime_flags.yaml and a smoke test in infra/ci/perf-runner.yaml.
Priya Rao: Did you run this on driver 525/535 combos? We had a flaky ordering problem before.
Ethan Kim: Yes - added a skip for driver < 535 and documented in third_party/nccl/notes.md. Verified on 535/540 images.
Ava Patel: Approved after minor nits fixed in comments.
discussion: Reviewer threads focused on avoiding global device sync and safe rollout. Early CI showed a transient failure on CUDA driver 520; we gated the new code on driver version and feature flags. The final CI pass used internal perf hardware; leads approved the performance numbers and the PR was squashed and merged.
benchmarks: throughput: +22% at target batching levels in production-like mix
